meta.note: written from the 2026 preseason composite projections (best legal lineup, taxi excluded), the 2025 results, and every trade and draft pick since the 2025 season ended

2.head: #2 projected · lineup WAR 8.86 · 3-yr 21.6 · avg starter age 28.2 · 2025: 12-2, champion
2.text: The champion, the highest three-year total in the league, and the oldest starting nine in it. Christian McCaffrey, Bijan Robinson, Ja'Marr Chase and Lamar Jackson are a title core for two more Januaries; Travis Kelce at 36 and Mike Evans at 33 are not, and the WR2 and WR3 seats — Malik Nabers and Jayden Reed at under half a win apiece — are the softest on any contender. The offseason did not touch that: Chuba Hubbard became a second-round rookie, Deebo Samuel became Aaron Jones, Adonai Mitchell became Kaleb Johnson. Tinkering. A repeat needs a real second receiver, and this roster still has the 2028 and 2029 firsts and the market's respect to go get one. Spend them before the decline shows up in the box score rather than after.

8.head: #1 projected · lineup WAR 9.17 · 3-yr 20.8 · avg starter age 26.1 · 2025: 10-4, 5th
8.text: The best lineup in the league on paper, and it got there by doing the hard thing: Saquon Barkley at 29 went out in the three-way deal and James Cook and Jauan Jennings came back, which is the right age swap at running back for a roster built around Jayden Daniels, Amon-Ra St. Brown and Brock Bowers. Marvin Harrison going out in the same deal is the part that could sting — a 24-year-old receiver is exactly what this team will be short of in two years. Every one of the nine seats projects positive and the core is 26. The bill is the cupboard: the 2027 and 2028 firsts and seconds are all gone, and the 2026 draft was one fourth-round flier. That is fine exactly as long as this team wins — a 10-4 season that ended fifth is the warning, and a repeat of it with no picks to sell would be the worst outcome on the board. The window is now, and it is not wide.

6.head: #3 projected · lineup WAR 7.84 · 3-yr 19.9 · avg starter age 26.4 · 2025: 12-2, runner-up
6.text: The most valuable roster in the league by market price, the runner-up at 12-2, and the only contender that made no trades at all. That is a choice, and the projections say it was the wrong one: third in lineup WAR behind two teams that moved, with Dak Prescott at 33 as the QB1 and Ashton Jeanty projecting well under what the market thinks he is. Puka Nacua and De'Von Achane are as good as any pair in the league, the 2028 and 2029 firsts are intact, and the draft was three late fliers. Sitting on the most tradable asset base in the room while the champion ages and the team above you goes all-in is how a runner-up becomes a bridesmaid. Cash something.

1.head: #4 projected · lineup WAR 7.82 · 3-yr 17.1 · avg starter age 26.3 · 2025: 8-6, 3rd
1.text: A 6-seed that got hot and finished third, and then bought like a champion: A.J. Brown and Chuba Hubbard for the 2027 first and second. Brown is 29 and the price was steep, but the two-quarterback room of Brock Purdy and Drake Maye is the youngest top-tier pair in the league and Trey McBride is the second-best tight end seat on any roster, so the case for pushing is real. The case against is the backfield — Josh Jacobs and Breece Hall at six-tenths of a win each, Travis Etienne behind them — which is a contender's weakest position by some distance. Fourth in projected WAR with a first still in hand for 2028 (Big Bucky Hunter's) and 2029: one more move at running back and this is a title roster. Without it, third again is the ceiling.

9.head: #5 projected · lineup WAR 6.88 · 3-yr 15.9 · avg starter age 27.8 · 2025: 10-4, 4th
9.text: Jahmyr Gibbs is the best running back seat in the league and Nico Collins is a WR1; that carried a 10-4 record and a fourth-place finish, and the market price says it will not carry much more — this roster is worth tenth of twelve. Matthew Stafford at 38, Joe Mixon at 30 and Dallas Goedert at 31 are the depth, and the tight end seat projects a quarter of a win. Ty Simpson at 1.09 is a sensible succession plan behind Justin Herbert, and holding every own first through 2029 is the right shape for a team whose window is Gibbs's legs. But no trade, no move at tight end, and an aging superflex seat means the record flattered the roster last year and the schedule will not do it twice.

10.head: #7 projected · lineup WAR 6.15 · 3-yr 13.4 · avg starter age 26.0 · 2025: 6-8, 8th
10.text: Caleb Williams and Bo Nix are the right foundation for a superflex league and both are on this roster; that is the reason to be patient. The rest is a reason not to be: Derrick Henry is 32 and should be sold this month, not next spring, and the receiver room past Jaylen Waddle is Garrett Wilson and Parker Washington. Five draft picks led by Germie Bernard at 1.10 and Kaytron Allen at 2.07 add bodies, not starters. The one trade of the offseason swapped Aaron Jones for Deebo Samuel, which is noise. Seventh in projected WAR is the right rank for a roster that is half built; whether it climbs depends on whether Henry's last good season gets converted into a 2027 first while it still can be.

11.head: #6 projected · lineup WAR 6.29 · 3-yr 13.3 · avg starter age 28.2 · 2025: 9-5, 6th
11.text: Three stars and six holes. Jalen Hurts, Jonathan Taylor and Jaxon Smith-Njigba are as good a top three as anyone fields; below them the tight end seat and the flex project at roughly nothing, Chris Godwin is a WR3 at a tenth of a win, and Terry McLaurin is 30. A three-year total of 13.3 is a middle-class number wearing a playoff team's record, and the 2027 first is already gone. KC Concepcion at 1.07 is a fair swing at the receiver problem; Isiah Pacheco on IR is not a fix at running back. The path back to the bracket runs through one real move at tight end or flex, and the assets to make it are the 2028 and 2029 firsts. Standing still is a 7-7 team.

12.head: #9 projected · lineup WAR 4.58 · 3-yr 9.1 · avg starter age 25.2 · 2025: 4-10, 9th
12.text: A 4-10 team that traded James Cook and Jauan Jennings and came back with Saquon Barkley and a 2027 first. The pick is the point and it is a good one — two 2027 firsts now, own and Unsolicited Nix pics's — but a rebuilding roster acquiring a 29-year-old running back is a plan with a clock on it; Barkley has to be flipped by the deadline or the return evaporates. The draft went receiver four times, Jordyn Tyson at 1.04 leading, and Tyson, Jayden Higgins, Christian Kirk and Tank Dell are all on IR, which is why Alec Pierce and Quentin Johnston are starting. Jaxson Dart is the right kind of quarterback to build on. Youngest lineup in the top nine; ninth in WAR; every dollar of value depends on what Barkley fetches in November.

3.head: #8 projected · lineup WAR 5.82 · 3-yr 10.5 · avg starter age 25.8 · 2025: 7-7, 7th
3.text: Fourth in market value, eighth in projected WAR, and the gap has one name: Malik Willis is the superflex starter. In a league where the second quarterback seat is the whole game, a 0.65-win projection there is the single biggest hole on any roster that expects to compete. The draft was seven picks, and the first of them was a tight end (Kenyon Sadiq at 1.08) for a roster that already had Colston Loveland — a luxury pick when the need was a quarterback, with Carson Beck at 3.06 as the consolation. Patrick Mahomes, Kenneth Walker, George Pickens and Loveland are a real core, and Bijan al-Gaib's 2027 first is a real chip. Turn the chips into a second quarterback and this is a playoff team; do not, and 7-7 is the median outcome again.

7.head: #10 projected · lineup WAR 3.37 · 3-yr 7.8 · avg starter age 25.1 · 2025: 4-10, 10th
7.text: Josh Allen and Joe Burrow are the two best quarterback seats in the league and they belong to the roster with the lowest market value in it. Three lineup seats project below zero — Denzel Boston, Adonai Mitchell and the flex — and the running back room is Omarion Hampton and then nothing. Six draft picks, Jadarian Price at 1.06 and Boston at 2.03, are the start of something; trading away the 2027 first before that something arrives is the kind of decision this roster cannot afford, and Kaleb Johnson for Adonai Mitchell is a lottery ticket for a lottery ticket. The honest read: two elite quarterbacks keep this out of last place, and nothing else on the roster is currently doing anything. Every one of those quarterback points is being spent on a receiver corps that gives them back.

4.head: #12 projected · lineup WAR 0.80 · 3-yr -2.3 · avg starter age 25.4 · 2025: 1-13, 11th
4.text: The only roster in the league projected to return negative WAR over the next three years, and both starting running backs project below zero on their own. That is the harsh part. The rest is a disciplined teardown: A.J. Brown was sold at 29 for a first and a second, Chuba Hubbard was bought for a second in February and flipped in the same package in August, the 2026 draft was seven picks with six in the first two rounds (Carnell Tate, Omar Cooper, Chris Bell, Eli Stowers, Malachi Fields, Nicholas Singleton), and four 2027 firsts are in hand with nothing traded away. Trevor Lawrence and Tyler Shough will not move the needle in superflex, and the quarterback seat is the one place the war chest has to go. Last place again is likely and, for once, it is the plan working.

5.head: #11 projected · lineup WAR 1.49 · 3-yr 3.2 · avg starter age 26.3 · 2025: 1-13, 12th
5.text: One and thirteen with the fewest points in the league's history, and the correct response to it: eight first-round picks in the next three drafts, four of them in 2027, and the 2026 class opened Jeremiyah Love, Fernando Mendoza and Makai Lemon at 1.01, 1.02 and 1.05 — paying a first and a second to move up one slot for the quarterback, which is what a superflex rebuild should pay for. Spending one of five 2027 firsts on Marvin Harrison at 24 fits the same timeline. The lineup is still eleventh: Sam Darnold, Rhamondre Stevenson, Darren Waller and Mike Gesicki are placeholders and should be treated as such. This is what a rebuild is supposed to look like from the outside. It will look like 3-11 from the inside for one more year, and that is the price.
